unresolvedTrails: qeynet: Vaughan or Maple is a current vendor address while Waterloo is a research origin; do not call either headquarters without proof, do not conflate this mission with QEYSSat, and do not imply an on-orbit result before launch and commissioning evidence.

qii-ai: The exact legal entity and Ocean Supercluster project outcome remain unresolved; attribute product and performance claims, and use the September 2024 announcement date rather than the stale 2023 date.

qinetiq-target-systems-canada: The current Ontario legal entity remains unresolved and the Canadian operation is owned by U.K.-based QinetiQ Group; the former federal entity was continued out in 2017, so keep legalName null and do not attribute the global portfolio to Canada.

qnx: QNX is a BlackBerry division and high-assurance embedded software layer, not a complete naval mission system or a Canadian Patrol Submarine Project award; certification and security claims remain configuration-specific.

qohash: Use the current Quebec City and Toronto footprint rather than the stale Montreal-only location; do not infer investor control, classified accreditation, deployment architecture or defence customers.
qoherent: The NATO cohort and DND research contract establish development activity, not operational NATO adoption; contract outcomes, benchmarks, supported hardware and accreditation remain unknown.

qorsa-corporation: Exact legal identity, post-acquisition ownership and the qorsa.com versus qorsalabs.com canonical relationship remain unresolved; no independently validated customer deployment or security accreditation is public.

qra-corp: The operating brand is QRA Corp while historical government material names QRA Consulting Inc.; keep legalName nullable until registry reconciliation and do not equate requirements-analysis tooling with certification or verification authority.

quantum-bridge-technologies: Use quantumbridge.io or qubridge.io as the current public surface rather than the stale quantumbridge.com and Halifax details; attribute unbreakable and TRL 9 language, and keep government-test results, ownership and accreditation unknown.

quaternion-aerospace: Exact legal identity, flight heritage, platform qualification and magnetic-anomaly-detection performance remain unresolved; Canadian grants establish development work, not operational deployment.

radiation-solutions: Public sources do not establish military adoption or configuration-level certification, and the operating and ownership effects of the RMS Instruments acquisition remain unresolved.

ranovus: RANOVUS supports semiconductor and AI-data-centre infrastructure rather than direct field communications; no precise recent material signal was recovered and production volume, yield, ownership and customer deployment remain unknown.

ravelin-dynamics: No independent company-specific proof was recovered; a Sentinel Shield submission and company-claimed NORAD, DRDC, NATO or Five Eyes engagement are not selection, customer relationships, validated performance or adoption.

rbr: RBR supplies environmental ocean sensing rather than sonar or target detection; an independent Argo report records unmet planned RBR adoption due uncertainty, and defence qualification and vehicle-integration details remain unknown.

reaction-dynamics: The Hanwha item is an exploratory memorandum and the 2026 and 2028 launch dates are forward-looking; no licensed or completed flight, launch service, customer or verified performance is public.

redlen-technologies: Redlen has been wholly owned by Japan's Canon since 2021 and is primarily a medical-imaging supplier; no recent material signal or public defence deployment was recovered, so bound relevance to radiological imaging, security and nondestructive testing.

rheinmetall-canada: Rheinmetall Canada is a subsidiary of German Rheinmetall AG; a display, demo or future first-delivery schedule does not establish CAF acceptance or operational fielding, and PATH performance, Canadian workshare and current capacity remain unresolved.

rocket-lab-space-systems-canada: The legal Canadian entity is Rocket Lab Space Systems Inc., a Toronto subsidiary of the U.S.-listed parent; keep the Canadian component operation distinct from the parent's launch portfolio and treat the medium-wheel award as development rather than qualification.

rockport-networks: Current registry evidence shows an active federal company, but a legacy compliance banner appears stale; do not infer dissolution. The DND-linked work is a research testbed, not deployed defence C2, and current sales, support and performance remain unresolved.

roshel: Ukraine support and newly unveiled vehicles do not establish CAF procurement or operational acceptance; configuration-specific protection certification, current capacity, Canadian content and beneficial ownership remain unresolved.

rutter: The 2026 ACOA contribution supports development for naval and Arctic use rather than CAF deployment; official oil-detection pages conflict on range, so keep model-specific detection, false-alarm, cyber and customer claims unresolved.

sanctuary-ai: The 2026 production deployment and performance measures are company-reported for an unnamed automotive customer; do not infer independent validation, defence deployment, safety certification, deployment scale or the autonomy-versus-teleoperation boundary.

sbquantum: CanadaBuys names 13717658 Canada Inc. while CIPO names 13717674 Canada Inc.; keep legalName and ownership nullable, and treat launch and commissioning as evaluation rather than validated in-orbit performance or a MagQuest win.

sdq-solutions-canada: SDQ is presented as the defence arm of Sanari Space rather than a proven separate corporation; ARCSIS maturity, classified-pipeline, Jammertest and network-performance claims remain vendor-authored until legal structure, customer, test and accreditation evidence is resolved.

sea-canada: The legal Canadian entity is SEA CAN Systems Inc., formerly JSK and wholly owned by U.K. Cohort plc; technology transfer and local manufacture remain in progress, and an implementation contract does not establish fleet acceptance.

seamatica-aerospace: No qualified 2025 or 2026 deployment, customer or certification signal was recovered; Chronos relies on cooperative transponder replies and active interrogation remains development-stage, so do not describe experimental or simulated capabilities as operational detect-and-avoid.

seamor-marine: The AquaEye integration project and a trade-show platform unveiling do not establish qualification, customer acceptance or military deployment; new-platform specifications, endurance, sea state, tether, launch-and-recovery and production capacity remain unknown.

seaspan-shipyards: Seaspan Shipyards is a Canadian operating division inside the privately held Seaspan and Washington Companies group with U.S. ultimate ownership; construction and trials do not establish accepted operational capability, and the JSS schedule retains delivery risk.

sedna-rov-services: Sedna is a distinct 100-percent Inuit-owned Iqaluit firm and must not be conflated with Sedna Technologies; civilian hydrography and dual-use funding do not establish a CAF operational contract, and asset delivery, USV performance and data quality remain unresolved.

sedna-technologies: The legal entity is Happy Fish Technologies Inc. operating as Sedna Technologies and is unrelated to Sedna ROV; fisheries and aquaculture software must not be inflated into defence C2 or maritime-domain awareness, and no current defence customer is public.

sensor-technology: The planned Collingwood facility and NRC-funded DAQ+P development do not establish commissioning, product readiness, customer acceptance or defence qualification; performance, customers and production output remain unknown.

sentinel-advanced-military-solutions: Sentinel is an operating brand or division within CMP Advanced Mechanical Solutions rather than a proven separate legal entity; broad ecosystem claims do not establish named mature products, contracts, tests, readiness or system-level accreditation.

sentinel-r-and-d: Product range, endurance, payload and NATO-standard language are vendor claims; the Ukraine arrangement does not establish production volume, flight validation or CAF adoption, and exact systems, capacity and certification remain unresolved.

simactive: The 2026 RDII contribution supports defence-market development rather than deployment; historical DND use from 2009 is not a current customer signal, and offline, classified, API, licensing and independent accuracy details remain unresolved.

simthetiq: The 2026 Boeing visual-system update is company-authored, and unnamed NATO-country and certified-worldwide claims remain attributed; do not infer participation in NATO distributed training or current accredited deployment.

skygauge-robotics: Use skygauge.com as the current canonical domain. Royal Canadian Navy trials do not establish adoption or procurement, and reported speed, coverage and success metrics remain vendor-authored pending test results, NDT approvals and ownership evidence.

skywatch-space-applications: Microsoft's listing is developer self-attestation rather than independent security certification; SkyWatch provides imagery access and tasking, not satellite operation or finished analytics, and data residency, licensing, SLA and defence customers remain unresolved.

slacan-industries: Government evidence supports electrical-grid manufacturing expansion rather than defence adoption; the mission connection is resilient critical infrastructure and industrial capacity, while ownership, capacity uplift, Controlled Goods status and defence qualification remain unknown.

solace: Solace's event middleware and agent orchestration do not establish defence hardening or operational C2 use; current control, security and classified posture, deployment boundaries and defence customers remain unresolved.

solana-networks: The DND award scope is undisclosed and must not be mapped to SmartHawk, SmartFlow or TrafficWiz without evidence; challenge, deliverables, interfaces, performance, accreditation and ownership remain unknown.

solarsteam: The current project is a demonstration of concentrated-solar process heat and liquid cooling, not general electrical generation; cold-weather performance, commissioning, storage, backup, manufacturing capacity and DIANA details remain unresolved.

space-engine-systems: No qualified 2026 deployment signal was recovered; TRL 6, Mach 5, ground-proven and airworthiness language remains company-authored and current workforce, financing, test results, customers and export posture are unresolved.

spacebridge: SpaceBridge Inc. is not a current Baylin subsidiary after the 2018 asset split; registry filings, ownership and assets require reconciliation, and additional-sales eligibility does not establish a defence customer, ruggedization, anti-jam capability or NGSO interoperability.

ssi-canada: SSi Micro Ltd. operating as SSi Canada has durable civilian and regulatory northern-network evidence, but the new defence and military-grade language is unsupported marketing; do not infer defence qualification, procurement, classified accreditation or current military customers.

Quanergy Solutions Canada: The current product owner is the United States company Quanergy Solutions Inc., created after a 2023 Chapter 11 asset sale, and no durable current Canadian legal entity, office, staff or operating footprint was recovered. The canonical Ottawa and Canadian-company identity is unsupported.

Safran Electronics & Defense Canada: Woodward acquired all equity of the Peterborough Safran Electronics & Defense Canada entity in July 2025 and supplier quality records identify its later name as Woodward Canada Inc. The canonical record also mixes that divested controls business with other Safran Canadian navigation and optronics activities.

Sierra Space Canada: Durable sources identify Sierra Space Corporation in Broomfield, Colorado, and no Canadian subsidiary, facility, employees or Canadian customer program was found. The stored Brampton address appears to belong to MDA Space rather than Sierra Space.

SkyX: The historical Canadian aerial pipeline-monitoring company has no qualified operating signal after 2022, current search results collide with an unrelated United States public company, and Investment Canada evidence indicates foreign control at formation. Current Canadian operation, ownership and customers remain unresolved.

Space Flight Laboratory: The University of Toronto Space Flight Laboratory became the private SFL Missions Inc. in May 2026, and a July CanadaBuys award now names SFL Missions Inc. The old university-lab canonical identity is stale and the exact corporate, intellectual-property and duplicate-record relationship requires a core lifecycle decision.

SpaceRyde: Deloitte records that SpaceRyde Inc. made an Assignment in Bankruptcy on February 10, 2023, the official domain no longer resolves, and the federal registry's administratively active status conflicts with overdue filings and an intent-to-dissolve notice. A current supplier dossier would be misleading.
